title: Arthur Godfrey sits in at the Edgewater Beach Hotel
summary: Godfrey, in Chicago with his horse, sits in with the band for two nights and praises Harry Shields.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Because Arthur Godfrey had, happened to be in Chicago for a week with his horse, Goldie. He has a horse that does tricks. This horse, his name is Goldie. And he happened to be in Chicago that week, staying at the Edgewater Beach Hotel. Because during the day, he was performing at a stock show. His horse was performing at a stock show. And he got, and Arthur Godfrey doesn't go anywhere without his banjo. And he has a beautiful, expensive banjo. And he flipped over the banjo. We were doing two shows a night in Chicago with the Edgewater Beach Hotel in the big, I forget the name of the room. But anyway, this room holds about 800 people. And he just flipped over the ban. And he wanted to know if he could sit in with us the next night. So he sat in with us, I think, two nights in a row in a floor show. Which we really enjoyed. And he invited us to go on his daily CBS radio show in New York, which in those days came on at 10 to 11 in the morning. But we never did get up there because we didn't, we didn't, we were, in those days, we were booked like seven months in advance, you know. But he was real nice. And he just flipped over old Harry Shields, the late Harry Shields. He loved Harry Shields. Loved his plan. He says, I like that old man. And he really bragged about old Harry Shields. Who was a very good player. And of course, as everyone knows, Harry Shields was the brother of the late Larry Shields. And Larry Shields passed away many years ago in California and was responsible for writing clarinet and marmalade, plus a whole flock of other tunes. I couldn't begin a name.
You know, Arthur Godfrey had some pretty good musicians with him at the time.
